question: Should OpenClaw adopt this shared localization runtime and release-readiness architecture as a core product direction, and if so should it land only as separately reviewed foundation slices?
rationale: The proposal introduces new cross-surface contracts, shared registry ownership, protocol metadata, and repository-wide promotion gates; correctness alone cannot choose whether that permanent product boundary is desired.

options.title: Sponsor a staged core rollout
options.body: Adopt the direction, require each foundation slice to become independently reviewable and compatible, and land only after proof for its user-visible surfaces.

options.title: Narrow to current localization fixes
options.body: Keep only concrete existing localization regressions and defer the shared runtime and release-readiness framework until a maintainer-approved design exists.

options.title: Keep the RFC under discussion
options.body: Leave the proposal draft while the RFC and ownership model are resolved before accepting implementation work.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a staged core rollout
recommendation.body: Adopt the direction, require each foundation slice to become independently reviewable and compatible, and land only after proof for its user-visible surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: The author owns the proposed five-part series and can supply its intended boundaries and proof, while a repository product owner must make the final direction decision.
